findingDispositions.assessment: Both recovery loops permit mixed 200/503 responses and check body state against each response status. The HTTP loop uses an exact safe body including empty advisories; the direct-handler loop checks the required status/database fields. Eventual all-ready observation still requires 32 responses, successful ready bodies and exactly one user-schema initialization, followed by authenticated identity success. The deterministic regression clones actual generated persistence into a unique import directory, samples 16 calls at t=249 and 16 at t=250, and observes false/true respectively with one customer-schema initialization. It exercises generated SQLite behavior rather than a duplicated readiness algorithm.
findingDispositions.limits: The deterministic regression is a generated-persistence boolean test, not a synchronized HTTP burst. HTTP status/body integration is covered by the corrected live suite. Outer recovery-loop budgets are polling checks, not proof of a hard response deadline.

findingDispositions.assessment: The initialization catch recognizes structured SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED and their underscore-prefixed extended variants as recoverable, so they report safe dependency unavailability without setting the fatal latch. The additional classification is local to initializePersistenceOnce; isPersistenceAvailabilityFailure and retryablePersistenceCause retain their existing rules. Real BEGIN EXCLUSIVE tests cover a lock present during initial import and a lock introduced during recovery after missing-path startup. Both remain nonfatal while locked and become ready after release. The live process test covers missing-directory and initial-exclusive-lock startup, observes liveness 200 and readiness/ordinary traffic 503, releases the obstruction, then observes readiness 200 and unmatched traffic 404 in the same process. Invalid signing configuration and incompatible auth schema continue to exit with safe startup diagnostics.
findingDispositions.limits: Real SQLite exclusive-lock coverage establishes native BUSY behavior; extended LOCKED variants are additionally checked with structured-code injection, not claimed as independently produced native lock modes. This does not review or broaden transaction replay.
